PHe0bXAIuk0.summary: Ray Dalio's 30-minute animated video explains how the economy works through credit, debt, interest rates, and short- and long-term cycles. It is based on his template for understanding the economy.
PHe0bXAIuk0.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the best layperson overview of debt, credit and economic cycles.

PUv66718DII.summary: Bret Victor's talk at CUSEC 2012 in which he argues that creators need immediate feedback and should organize their work around a guiding principle. He demonstrates live-coding and animation tools that show results as you type, and describes his own principle that creators must see what they are making.
PUv66718DII.why: It is HN's go-to recommendation for the case that programming environments should give instant feedback, and it appears in nearly every thread on live coding, visual programming or developer tools.

PmTUW-owa2w.summary: Innuendo Studios uses Phil Fish, creator of the game Fez, as a case study in internet celebrity. The essay argues that fame online works differently from traditional fame, and shows how audiences turn on the people they have elevated.
PmTUW-owa2w.why: Commenters repeatedly name it the best explanation of how internet fame, mobs and outrage work, and cite it in threads about harassment and public figures.

PGLYEDpNu60.summary: Richard Cook's short Velocity 2013 talk on resilience in complex adaptive systems, arguing systems operate near the edge of failure and that the surprise is how rarely they fail. He presents a model of how pressures push systems toward failure boundaries.
PGLYEDpNu60.why: HN people cite it constantly as the clearest explanation of normalization of deviance and how complex systems drift toward failure.

P-2P3MSZrBM.summary: Lex Fridman has a three-hour conversation with Joscha Bach about artificial consciousness, the workings of the mind, intelligence and the possibly simulated nature of reality.
P-2P3MSZrBM.why: Praised as a long but rewarding conversation, with commenters especially liking Bach's emphasis on modelling as a skill and his bridge between mind and computation.

PFDu9oVAE-g.summary: 3Blue1Brown's chapter on eigenvectors and eigenvalues in the Essence of Linear Algebra series. It builds a visual intuition for what they mean, why an eigenbasis is useful, and ends with a puzzle.
PFDu9oVAE-g.why: HN repeatedly names it the best, most intuitive explanation of eigenvalues, and a gateway to the whole linear algebra series.

PorfLSr3DDI.summary: Greg Law's 15-minute CppCon 2015 lightning talk shows what GDB can do beyond basic use, including its text user interface and reverse debugging.
PorfLSr3DDI.why: Recommended as a fast, brilliant introduction to GDB's TUI mode and lesser-known features, useful for anyone who has only used IDE debuggers.

PqPGOhXoprU.summary: Jack Szostak's lecture covers how cellular life could have arisen from chemistry on the early Earth, starting from the odds of life elsewhere in the galaxy. It is part of a series on protocells and the RNA world.
PqPGOhXoprU.why: Recommended as a clear, authoritative lecture series on plausible origin-of-life theories.

PQmSUHhP3ug.summary: Onboard footage of Timo Bernhard driving the Porsche 919 Hybrid Evo to an all-time Nurburgring Nordschleife record lap of 5:19.
PQmSUHhP3ug.why: HN cites it as the benchmark lap record and recommends it even to non-car fans for its sheer speed and precision.

PfYYraMgiBA.summary: Irving Finkel of the British Museum lectures at the Royal Institution on the invention and decipherment of cuneiform writing in Mesopotamia, and why it is so hard to translate.
PfYYraMgiBA.why: HN users recommend it as a delightful, well-told account of how cuneiform developed and was decoded.

P3AyI_u66Bw.summary: Larry Hastings explains what Python's GIL is, what problems it solves and how it works, and presents his Gilectomy project to remove it, including the performance and C-extension obstacles.
P3AyI_u66Bw.why: The default reference in Python performance threads for why removing the GIL is hard.

PE4gwstWhmc.summary: Dropbox engineer Kevin Modzelewski gives a Stanford colloquium on Dropbox's history and the technical problems it faced scaling, including detailed database schema decisions.
PE4gwstWhmc.why: Recommended as a detailed, candid case study of scaling a real system from zero users to millions.

PJy8vTu66tE.summary: Harvard law professor Lawrence Lessig argues that US democracy is corrupted by money, since a tiny fraction of the population effectively funds who gets elected. He says fixing this must come before addressing issues like climate change or student debt.
PJy8vTu66tE.why: It is HN's go-to link in threads on lobbying, campaign finance and political dysfunction, as a clear statement of Lessig's root-cause argument.

Pi7l8mMjYVE.summary: The opening lecture of Steve Brunton's Control Bootcamp, covering the kinds of control and why closed-loop feedback matters. It starts a series that follows the control chapter of the Brunton and Kutz data-driven science book.
Pi7l8mMjYVE.why: HN recommends the series as an approachable but rigorous way to learn control theory, with good production quality.

PhhC_N6Bm_s.summary: David Foster Wallace's 2005 commencement speech at Kenyon College, about the default settings of the mind, choosing what to pay attention to, and what we end up worshipping.
PhhC_N6Bm_s.why: HN people point lost, lonely or burned-out readers to it as a short, humane piece of perspective on how to live.

Pld8wTa16Jk.summary: An Isaac Arthur episode on civilizations in the far future, past the Black Hole Era. It covers iron stars, Boltzmann brains, reversible computing and the idea of reversing entropy.
Pld8wTa16Jk.why: HN recommends Isaac Arthur as an entry point for far-future and thermodynamic-endgame questions.

Pp9MwZkHiMQ.summary: Benn Jordan explains how Flock Safety's license plate cameras log and share vehicle locations, and explores how adversarial AI can defeat them. It covers weak security and the surveillance risks of private police-camera networks.
Pp9MwZkHiMQ.why: HN treats it as the go-to overview of Flock's problems, and cites it in nearly every Flock thread.

Pzl1B7nB9Kc.summary: Excerpts from Linus Torvalds's DebConf 14 talk on why desktop Linux struggles. He covers application distribution, distros breaking backwards compatibility, wasted package management effort and how Windows does app distribution better.
Pzl1B7nB9Kc.why: Cited constantly in Flatpak, packaging and ABI-compatibility debates as Linus's blunt, insightful take on shipping software for Linux.

P55t6eryY3g.summary: A video essay from the Alt-Right Playbook series that explains how extremist movements draw ordinary people in, using deniable rhetoric, bad-faith games, and gradual escalation. It draws on books about the alt-right, male radicalization, and cult-style brainwashing.
P55t6eryY3g.why: HN commenters cite it in moderation and politics threads as a clear account of why hard rules fail against dogwhistles and how isolated people get recruited.

P73REgj-3UE.summary: The Primitive Technology channel shows the construction of a tiled roof hut in the bush using only primitive tools and materials made in earlier videos. It includes tiles, a kiln, clay walls and underfloor heating.
P73REgj-3UE.why: HN shares it as a mesmerizing example of building shelter and tools entirely from scratch.

P9M__yYbsZ4.summary: A 2011 remix of over six hours of talks by Kirk Sorensen and other thorium advocates, explaining thorium as a nuclear fuel and the liquid-fluoride thorium reactor (LFTR). It argues LFTRs could produce energy without long-lived transuranic waste.
P9M__yYbsZ4.why: HN users send it to anyone asking about thorium or molten salt reactors as a compact overview that answers common anti-nuclear objections.

PLyEO0jNt6M.summary: Mick West analyzes the Navy "Go Fast" UFO footage and shows with simple trigonometry and the data overlay that the object is slow and high up, consistent with a balloon. He explains how parallax makes it look fast and argues the original TV claims were wrong.
PLyEO0jNt6M.why: HN commenters repeatedly cite it as a checkable, math-based debunking of the famous UFO clips whenever UAP stories come up.

PY9DcIMGxMs.summary: Johann Hari's TED talk arguing that addiction is driven largely by disconnection and environment rather than chemical hooks alone. He draws on his personal experience with addicted relatives and on research and policy examples from around the world.
PY9DcIMGxMs.why: HN commenters quote it for the line that the opposite of addiction is connection, and recommend it as a more plausible account of addiction than the standard model.

PbmJkMhmrVI.summary: Physicist Angela Collier argues that dark matter is not a theory but a set of observations, covering rotation curves, the CMB and why modified gravity struggles to explain them.
PbmJkMhmrVI.why: HN links it to correct the common misconception about dark matter and as a counterpoint to popular science coverage, though one commenter found it muddled.

PIPjmmmh_os.summary: Slavoj Zizek and Paul Holdengraber discuss surveillance and whistleblowers at the International Authors' Stage, ranging over Snowden, Assange, Pussy Riot and humor.
PIPjmmmh_os.why: HN commenters call it an entertaining, complementary philosophical take on surveillance, with a funny story about jamming secret police.

PJnJ8mK3Q3g.summary: Climate Town gives a comedic, fast-paced account of how the plastics industry promoted recycling, including the resin-code recycling symbol, while knowing most plastic could not be economically recycled. It points viewers to the Frontline documentary Plastic Wars for a deeper treatment.
PJnJ8mK3Q3g.why: Commenters send it as a short, entertaining explanation of why people believe plastic is recyclable and how industry PR created that belief.

PQccNdwm8Tw.summary: A conference presentation by Bert Hubert on how companies lose their technological edge and become outsourcing hubs. It argues the same dynamic applies to whole countries and continents, and ends with suggestions for reversing it.
PQccNdwm8Tw.why: HN points to it as a sharper explanation of why outsourcing and specialization erode deep expertise, in threads on Intel, Boeing and software decline.

PYylPRX6z4Q.summary: Robert Miles explains reward modelling, in which an AI learns what humans want from their preference comparisons instead of a hand-written reward function. He walks through the 2017 paper on deep reinforcement learning from human preferences.
PYylPRX6z4Q.why: Seen as the clearest introduction to the idea behind RLHF, and also borrowed by commenters as a metaphor for human motivation.

PZbqAMEwtOE.summary: A New York Times Op-Docs short in which actors perform a real legal deposition transcript. A lawyer gets tangled in an absurd argument with a county employee about what counts as a photocopier, in a dispute over fees for public records.
PZbqAMEwtOE.why: Commenters share it as a funny, memorable example of evasive depositions and of obstruction over public records requests.

PdO3IP0Pro8.summary: NativLang's 47-minute animated documentary traces the birth and evolution of writing, from early cave marks to modern scripts. It presents the history of the world's writing systems as a story.
PdO3IP0Pro8.why: HN recommends it as a fun, amazing overview of writing systems whenever the alphabet or cuneiform comes up.

Ps8jOj7diA0.summary: The first lecture of Stanford's CS107 Programming Paradigms, taught by Jerry Cain, giving an overview of the course. The course goes from C and assembly through C++, concurrency, Scheme and Python.
Ps8jOj7diA0.why: Commenters rate the whole playlist as high-quality, clear teaching that builds foundations from memory and machine instructions up to different paradigms.

PBFPJ3_6ZWs.summary: Technology Connections experiments with filtering white and colored LEDs to make holiday lights look less garish. He explains why narrowband LED strings look harsh compared with incandescent bulbs.
PBFPJ3_6ZWs.why: HN links it in any LED Christmas light discussion as the explanation of why they look off and how to fix it.

PDylgzybWAw.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on payday loans and predatory lending, covering how they trap borrowers and target the elderly and military. It features Sarah Silverman.
PDylgzybWAw.why: HN recommends it as a good overview of predatory lending and the problems with payday loans.

PFUZlNQIndo.summary: Mark Raasveldt of CWI presents DuckDB, an embeddable analytical database described as the SQLite for analytics, in a CMU Database Group talk. He explains why it was built, what it is for, and how it works.
PFUZlNQIndo.why: HN recommends it as the definitive talk from the implementer on DuckDB's motivation and design.

PFc379hu--8.summary: Alan Kay visits Carnegie Mellon's School of Computer Science in 2007 for an informal conversation with faculty and students. He discusses the state of CS education and criticizes mainstream computing.
PFc379hu--8.why: HN recommends it for Kay's blunt critique of today's computing and standard CS curricula.

PSGEjv3Tqo0.summary: Douglas Crockford's Nordic.js 2014 talk on 'the better parts' of JavaScript and programming in general. He argues against `this`, `new` and ES6 classes, and for classless, composition-based object patterns, with some broader remarks on building better structures for the future.
PSGEjv3Tqo0.why: HN commenters cite it whenever JavaScript classes, `this` or inheritance come up, as the clearest case for classless OOP from Crockford.

PmlRbfSavbI.summary: Mark Rober and Jabril build an app that uses machine learning to decode baseball sign sequences. The video also explains neural networks in a simple, accessible way.
PmlRbfSavbI.why: Recommended as a fun, semi-technical intro to machine learning that holds kids' attention.

PpG0z-npFIY.summary: Kedi is a feature documentary following seven street cats of Istanbul and the people who care for them. It portrays the relationship between the city and its cats.
PpG0z-npFIY.why: HN users recommend it as a moving, heartwarming film whenever Istanbul's cats or cat history come up.

P1ww1IXRfTA.summary: All six episodes of the 1983 BBC series Fun to Imagine, in which Richard Feynman muses on jiggling atoms, fire, rubber bands, magnets, electricity and more. He explains how to think about nature and why imagination is fun.
P1ww1IXRfTA.why: HN recommends it for Feynman's intuitive explanations and his joy in understanding how things work.

PGv5BqNL164.summary: A WGBH/NOVA re-enactment of Clifford Stoll's hunt for KGB-linked hacker Markus Hess, based on his book The Cuckoo's Egg. It starts from a 75-cent accounting discrepancy at Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory.
PGv5BqNL164.why: Mentioned alongside The Cuckoo's Egg as the screen version of an early computer-security detective story.

PaCmpygFfXo.summary: Andrej Karpathy builds a bigram character-level language model from scratch, introducing torch.Tensor and the framework of training, sampling and loss evaluation. It is the first step toward a GPT-style Transformer in his makemore series.
PaCmpygFfXo.why: HN recommends it as a long but worthwhile way to demystify how language models work technically.

PbC4gqZGPSY.summary: A two-minute video of Ira Glass on the creative process, describing the gap between taste and skill when starting out and urging you to keep producing until your work matches your taste.
PbC4gqZGPSY.why: Shared as encouragement for beginners learning design or craft, on persisting through the taste-skill gap.

PezlFNTGWv4.summary: A clip from Charlie Brooker's Newswipe in which a forensic psychiatrist argues that intense news coverage of school shooters encourages copycat attacks, alongside Brooker's satire of formulaic news reporting.
PezlFNTGWv4.why: HN cites it in discussions about how media should report mass shootings, as an expert-backed argument for not glorifying perpetrators.

Phl82D57P58.summary: A short film of Alex Honnold free soloing El Sendero Luminoso, a 2,500-foot route in El Potrero Chico, Mexico, in a little over three hours with no rope. It was made by The North Face with climbing footage and music.
Phl82D57P58.why: It is linked whenever Honnold or free soloing comes up, as a gripping and frightening example of extreme climbing.

PnbOWi6f_IM.summary: The first part of a four-part Channel 4 (UK) documentary series presented by Howard Goodall, this episode covers melody and why tunes affect us so deeply. It explains how melody works in Western music with historical background and music theory.
PnbOWi6f_IM.why: HN people recommend the series as a good, approachable introduction to music theory with historical context.

PriwCi6SzLo.summary: Medlife Crisis asks whether academic research should sit behind paywalls, covering publisher profit margins, unpaid reviewers, Sci-Hub and Aaron Swartz. It includes an interview with Sci-Hub founder Alexandra Elbakyan.
PriwCi6SzLo.why: HN recommends it as an informative review of the academic publishing business and its monopoly-like structure.

PsPX0nElJ0k.summary: A short demo of Code Bubbles, an IDE interface built around editable code fragments in bubbles instead of files. It was a research prototype for Java development.
PsPX0nElJ0k.why: HN keeps returning to it as the most convincing example of moving past file-based code editing, even though it never left prototype stage.

PtKhbbcc1Rc.summary: Matt Parker of Stand-up Maths asks whether a country's reported land area accounts for hills and mountains, working through how surface area depends on the resolution of elevation data. It follows up on a question from a viewer and work by researchers who measured it.
PtKhbbcc1Rc.why: HN recommends it in map projection and coastline threads as a fun look at how measurement choices change area figures.

P4VBqTViEx4.summary: A three-minute excerpt of a Steve Jobs interview in which he describes how monopolies let sales and marketing people displace product people, rotting a company's product sensibility, with Xerox as the example.
P4VBqTViEx4.why: Cited constantly on HN whenever a large company declines, as the canonical explanation of product people being pushed out by sales and marketing.

P76Vbsk_3J0.summary: Rich Hickey introduces Clojure to the NYC Java Study Group in the first of a two-part talk. It covers reader syntax, core data structures, code-as-data, evaluation, special operators, functions, macros and sequences, assuming no Lisp background.
P76Vbsk_3J0.why: Recommended as a clear, well-paced introduction to Clojure and Lisp ideas like code as data and macros, straight from the language's creator.

PNbkv_DJ0f0.summary: A tool-assisted speedrun of Ocarina of Time at Summer Games Done Quick 2022, using TASBot and arbitrary code execution to reach an alternate ending in about 53 minutes. The run is introduced by its creators and followed by an interview.
PNbkv_DJ0f0.why: HN points to it as a stunning demonstration of arbitrary code execution in a console game and of what speedrunners effectively do as vulnerability researchers.

P_fHJIYENdI.summary: A Veritasium video on AlphaFold, DeepMind's protein structure prediction system, and the protein design work it enabled. It features interviews with John Jumper and with David Baker's protein design group and explains why predicting protein folding matters.
P_fHJIYENdI.why: HN points to it as an accessible explainer of AlphaFold and as an example of narrow, specialized ML delivering real scientific breakthroughs.

Pae2AMnmUVA.summary: Paul Taylor's first stand-up special, recorded in Paris in 2018, in which a British comedian living in France riffs on French culture, language and bureaucracy. It is the full 70-minute show.
Pae2AMnmUVA.why: Recommended as hilarious for anyone familiar with both French and British or American culture, and relevant to expats.

PaypcVFPs48.summary: Part 10 of Dan Gelbart's prototype-building lecture series, covering flexures: flexible joints that give precise, frictionless motion. It shows how a cheap piece of aluminum can become a nanometer-accurate mechanism.
PaypcVFPs48.why: HN recommends the series as a fascinating, practical course in precision prototyping, with the flexure episode singled out as especially impressive.

PlJkgQZb0VU.summary: Brian Springer's documentary Spin, built entirely from unauthorized satellite feeds of politicians and newscasters before they went on air during the 1992 US presidential election. It exposes the behind-the-scenes construction of media reality.
PlJkgQZb0VU.why: Recommended as a revealing look at how politicians and news anchors behave off camera and how packaged news feeds were produced.

PsXFwy6gG_4.summary: A 2012 Fortune dinner debate between Peter Thiel and Eric Schmidt over whether technological progress is healthy or stalling and whether Google can still innovate.
PsXFwy6gG_4.why: HN recalls it as one of the most interesting debates between two contrasting worldviews on progress.

PsgBtOVzHKI.summary: Part one of a four-part upload of a BBC Horizon documentary featuring Richard Feynman, in which he talks about physics and looking at the world from another point of view.
PsgBtOVzHKI.why: Mentioned as a fun and impressive Feynman documentary, though the mentions are brief.

P1IcaBn3ej0.summary: A video presenting an Intel research paper on enhancing the photorealism of synthetic images. A convolutional network uses rendering intermediates, shown on GTA V footage that comes out looking like real street scenes.
P1IcaBn3ej0.why: Used as a go-to example of neural networks enhancing game rendering, referenced in later AI-graphics discussions.

PC2JOQ7z5L0.summary: PBS Space Time explains Roger Penrose's conformal cyclic cosmology, in which the far future of our universe becomes the big bang of the next. It explores what could come after the universe ends.
PC2JOQ7z5L0.why: HN recommends it as a clearer explanation of Penrose's cyclic cosmology than comment threads can give.

PDL_pIPScSI.summary: Footage of a Minuteman III ICBM test launch and its reentry vehicles striking the Kwajalein atoll target area. It shows the missile climbing through clouds and the warheads descending.
PDL_pIPScSI.why: Linked as unusually clear real footage of ICBM reentries and impacts whenever missile tests or the Marshall Islands come up.

PHiyQID7SBs.summary: PBS Space Time explains the Standard Model Lagrangian, the single equation encapsulating the particle physics theory, and visualizes what its terms mean.
PHiyQID7SBs.why: Recommended as a good visual walkthrough of the Standard Model equation for people who want to understand its terms.

PTUY16CkS-k.summary: An animated xtranormal explainer on quantitative easing, what the Federal Reserve was doing and how things got there. It was made by Omid Malekan.
PTUY16CkS-k.why: HN pointed to it in 2011 as a nice, tongue-in-cheek explanation of quantitative easing.

PZRI1IfStY0.summary: Tom Scott explains for Computerphile how floating point numbers work, why moving the binary point is fast, and why it handles money badly.
PZRI1IfStY0.why: Recommended as a simple, fun explanation of why floating point gives odd errors like 0.1 + 0.2.

PaKIZ7gJlRU.summary: A short TFiR clip of Linus Torvalds explaining why he thinks GPLv3 violates what GPLv2 stood for. He describes why he chose GPLv2 for kernel development and his view of the FSF's approach.
PaKIZ7gJlRU.why: Cited again and again in GPL licensing debates as the primary source for Linus's objections to GPLv3.

Pm8P4oCIY3g.summary: Bryan Cantrill's talk on corporate open source anti-patterns, first given at FISL 2012 and again at the Liferay Symposium. He lays out the mistakes companies make when open sourcing code, such as announcing future open sourcing, and discusses licenses.
Pm8P4oCIY3g.why: HN commenters invoke it whenever a company relicenses, forks, or announces an open source plan, and enjoy Cantrill's energetic, opinionated delivery.

PAAkCSZUG1c.summary: Rob Pike presents Go Proverbs at Gopherfest 2015, a set of pithy aphorisms about Go design such as 'Clear is better than clever' and 'A little copying is better than a little dependency'.
PAAkCSZUG1c.why: HN treats it as the canonical source for Go proverbs, quoted in debates about dependencies, concurrency and simplicity.

PGqCeSjNuTY.summary: David Shaw of D. E. Shaw Research presents Anton, a special-purpose machine that speeds up biomolecular simulations about a hundred-fold. The lecture covers molecular dynamics and how simulation helps understand how drugs bind.
PGqCeSjNuTY.why: HN points to it as an accessible, interesting talk on molecular dynamics and simulation-based drug discovery.

PnpX8d8zRIA.summary: Technology Connections gives a deeply researched history of RCA's CED video disc system, a capacitance-based format that took over a decade to reach market. Part one covers its development and strange technology.
PnpX8d8zRIA.why: HN praises the depth of research and uses the CED story as a case study of a mismanaged, badly timed product.

P0ukYf_xvgc.summary: Kevin Spacey, giving the MacTaggart Lecture at the Edinburgh Television Festival, urges TV channels to give viewers control. He points to Netflix's House of Cards release as evidence that audiences want to watch on their own terms.
P0ukYf_xvgc.why: HN cites it in streaming and piracy threads as an argument that giving viewers control is how to compete.

P7GKK3liv8M.summary: Tom Scott, who never learned to ride a bike, gets lessons from Mike Boyd, a YouTuber known for learning skills quickly. The video follows an adult's attempt to learn cycling in a short time.
P7GKK3liv8M.why: HN uses it as the go-to example of an adult learning to ride a bike, mostly in threads about learning cycling later in life.

P8pjd1QEA0c.summary: John Oliver covers student debt and the for-profit colleges that push students into it, including Corinthian-style schools and ITT Tech. It is a segment from Last Week Tonight.
P8pjd1QEA0c.why: HN mostly references it in passing when student loans and predatory colleges come up, with one commenter recommending the veterans benefits section.

PDBiLT3LASk.summary: A one-minute clip of Sir Thomas More's speech from 'A Man for All Seasons', defending giving even the devil the benefit of the law. The uploader ties it to debates about torture and extralegal action.
PDBiLT3LASk.why: Quoted whenever HN debates due process and legal protections, even for people one dislikes.

PM2RxWtF4Ds.summary: Tony Seba of RethinkX presents the case that solar, wind and batteries are on a cost-decline path that makes a fully renewable grid achievable. It was made for the Global 100% RE Strategy Group's joint declaration.
PM2RxWtF4Ds.why: HN cites it as support for the argument that renewables with storage are already cheapest and still getting cheaper.

PMotykw0SIk.summary: Chamath Palihapitiya's Stanford GSB View From The Top talk on money as an instrument of change. HN mostly knows it for his remarks on social media's dopamine-driven feedback loops and regrets about Facebook.
PMotykw0SIk.why: HN cites it in social media threads as a former Facebook executive's criticism of the platform.

PRa6t_e7dgI.summary: A short 60 Minutes clip from March 2020 in which Dr. Anthony Fauci tells Jon LaPook there is no reason to walk around wearing a mask. The full interview includes his concern about mask shortages for healthcare workers.
PRa6t_e7dgI.why: HN uses it as a flashpoint in arguments about early pandemic mask guidance, with critics citing the headline and defenders pointing to the shortage context.

PYmi0DLzBdQ.summary: A short clip, titled Orwell Comes to America, on reasoning and perception. One HN user links it repeatedly as the science showing human minds are bad at reasoning and do not see reality as it is.
PYmi0DLzBdQ.why: Almost entirely one commenter's repeated citation as evidence on unconscious thinking and flawed reasoning.

PhNUjg9X4g8.summary: A short Great Big Story piece about Hagoromo, a Japanese chalk brand so prized that mathematicians stockpiled it, with some reportedly dealing it on the side. It tells the quirky tale of a writing tool whose supply became scarce.
PhNUjg9X4g8.why: Cited as an amusing side story whenever HN discusses blackboards, chalk, and how mathematicians work.

PiGkzgfR_c0.summary: Cirrus introduces Safe Return, an emergency autoland system for its Vision Jet. A passenger presses a single button and the aircraft squawks emergency, reroutes and lands itself.
PiGkzgfR_c0.why: HN points to it as a real example of certified emergency autoland, used in debates about autonomy and pilotless aircraft.

Pot9GnHFOVU.summary: Tudor Girba's Curry On! 2019 talk on moldable development, the idea that developers should build custom tools and views for each software system they work on. It draws on the Pharo and Glamorous Toolkit environments.
Pot9GnHFOVU.why: HN cites it as the clearest pitch for programmable, malleable development environments, especially in threads on Smalltalk, Emacs and user-programmable systems.

Pp9Yax8UNoM.summary: A two-minute clip recorded on a Kennedy Space Center tour showing a Space Shuttle thermal tile that can be held by hand while its surface is extremely hot. It demonstrates the tile's remarkable insulating properties.
Pp9Yax8UNoM.why: Cited as a striking, counterintuitive example of extreme thermal insulation and hard materials science.

P8ijiLqfXP0.summary: A short Guardian clip of historian Rutger Bregman at Davos telling attendees that the real issue is tax avoidance, not philanthropy schemes.
P8ijiLqfXP0.why: Cited as an example of calling out billionaire philanthropy and tax avoidance in threads on wealth inequality.

P9yruQM1ggc.summary: A short Simpsons clip in which Principal Skinner explains the cycle of introducing a new species to deal with a previous pest. It is a joke about ecological interventions that backfire.
P9yruQM1ggc.why: It is posted as a punchline in threads about invasive species, pests and well-meant environmental fixes with side effects.

PF7EpEnglgk.summary: An episode of REACT in which children try to figure out 1970s-1980s computers, including an Apple II and floppy disks. It was made to promote the AMC show Halt and Catch Fire.
PF7EpEnglgk.why: Cited in discussions of intuitive design and how younger people relate to old technology.

PH1BKPSGcxQ.summary: TheRasteri upgrades a single PC through every Windows version, from early releases through Windows 10, testing that old software keeps running. It is an updated version of the Chain of Fools experiment.
PH1BKPSGcxQ.why: HN cites it as a demonstration of Windows' long backwards compatibility.

PH_Z8Ghuq6E.summary: A two-minute video of an athlete sprinting against a London Underground Circle Line train between Mansion House and Cannon Street. It shows a runner keeping pace with and beating the train.
PH_Z8Ghuq6E.why: Cited as proof that a fit person can outrun a Tube train over short distances.

PI_Jl5WFQkA.summary: The Canyonero song from The Simpsons episode The Last Temptation of Krust, a jingle parodying oversized SUV marketing.
PI_Jl5WFQkA.why: HN invokes it as a joke whenever large SUVs, trucks or the Cybertruck come up.

PSxihhBzCjk.summary: The famous scene from The Graduate in which a family friend gives Benjamin the career advice 'one word: plastics'. It is a roughly one-minute film clip.
PSxihhBzCjk.why: Used as a joke or shorthand reference when HN discusses the next big technology or career trend.

PV4Oze9JEU0.summary: A short edited clip from Star Trek: First Contact in which Captain Picard explains that humanity of the future no longer works for money or possessions. Added context frames the second part of the clip.
PV4Oze9JEU0.why: HN uses it as shorthand for post-scarcity economics, typically as a contrast to money-driven projects like crypto.

PX9reO3QnUA.summary: A short CNN news segment reporting on Donald Trump mocking a New York Times reporter who has a chronic condition during the 2015 campaign.
